string2: These entries, called strings, are here to guide you through some of the editor features.
string3: Try translating one and hitting TAB to save and move to the next string in the list.
string6: Another cool feature is filtering in the editor! Try typing 'Strings can hold' in the biginput with the magnifier on the left side - holding the strings list -.
string7: If 'Strings can hold %s variables too!' is translated, press Ctrl+2
string8: Hey there is a dark mode available too! Click the gear and then Editor preferences to select that!
string9: Each string also has additional context information, where you can see things like it's key - unique identifier - for that string, words size, tags and more.
string10: Translation Memory (TM), which is a pool of all your translations, is accessible via the Suggestions tab and Concordance. Through concordance you can search across all your entries.
string11: You can also add a Glossary, that you can populate with terms and see those terms in the editor for reference! Click Ctrl+4 to see the Glossary tab.
string12: Since more people can work on the same editor you can also collaborate using comments on a specific string. Click Ctrl+5 to see the Comments tab. You can add a comment or an issue.
string13: So far we've missed the Ctrl+2 shortcut, which will focus on the String History tab, containing information about each string. Like when it was created and when each translation was added.
string14: Last but not least, you can even edit the source content of a string for file formats like this one, which is key-value based. To do that, click on the 'Edit Source' link next to the languages selection.
string15: There are many more things to explore in the editor! Have a spin at your own or read more in our docs at: https://help.transifex.com/en/articles/6318216-translating-with-the-web-editor
string16: If you are have an app using key-value json files for your content. Try getting and uploading that json file from your team to continue!
string17: To clear the 'Strings can hold %s variables too!' filter, you can either delete everything inside the input with the magnifier or press the X located in the input box.
